next.name: GOLD LOCUST
next.headline: GOLD LOCUST, also tracked as FIN7 and Carbanak: mailed USB drives and loader malware
next.in_short: Secureworks tracks GOLD LOCUST, known under names including FIN7 and Carbanak. Reports describe mailed USB drives, the JSSLoader malware, and tools that vendors tie to the group.

sentences.t: Secureworks tracks this actor as GOLD LOCUST. Its catalogue record lists the aliases Anunak, Carbanak, Carbon Spider, FIN7 and Silicon.
The catalogue record names Carbanak as a tool of the group.
Morphisec Labs says it has tracked FIN7 (Carbanak Group) activity for several years.
A CSO Online article on Evil Corp says that group collaborated with other cybercriminal groups, including Carbanak/FIN7 and TA505.
An FBI alert, as reported by BleepingComputer, says FIN7 mailed packages to retail, restaurant and hotel businesses. The alert says the targets included HR, IT and executive staff.
BleepingComputer reports that in 2018 FIN7 hacked Saks Fifth Avenue and Lord & Taylor to steal payment card information.
The FBI alert describes USB drives sent by US mail. The drives act as keyboards and launch PowerShell commands that fetch GRIFFON malware.
One package was described as allegedly from Best Buy. It held a USB drive offered with a gift card.
The same report says the tools in these attacks include Metasploit, Cobalt Strike and Carbanak.
Morphisec describes a chain that starts with a phishing email. VBScript stages run in memory, and a scheduled task with a timeout delay launches the next step.
In that chain, the JSSLoader .NET trojan runs a script that loads Carbanak reflectively. Morphisec says the command server's hosting provider had been used by FIN7 before.
Malwarebytes describes a newer JSSLoader as a rewrite with more capabilities, including data exfiltration. It also drops a second payload written in .NET.
Morphisec says it intercepted its JSSLoader attack chain in a customer's network in December 2020.
In a post dated 15 August 2022, Malwarebytes attributed a late-June malspam campaign to FIN7.
SentinelLABS published a report on 3 November 2022. It says Black Basta ransomware attacks deployed custom EDR evasion tools that it ties to FIN7.

Harfanglab says Sentinel Labs links sellers of the AvNeutralizer anti-EDR tool to the FIN7 cluster with high confidence. Harfanglab adds that the PackXOR packer is used for activity unrelated to FIN7.
Rapid7 (report dated 10 June 2025) assesses that the developers of a Java malware family are likely initial access brokers. It says they may have provided access to Black Basta or FIN7 affiliates.
Treat unexpected USB drives and unsolicited invoice attachments as hostile. Do not plug them in or open them.
